subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT contain time t?
questions.explain: v² = u² + 2as relates velocity, acceleration and displacement without t.

questions.q: A 12 V supply is connected across a 6.0 Ω resistor. The power dissipated is:
A car travels at constant velocity along a straight road. What can be said about the forces on it?
options: There is a net forward force
The driving force equals the total resistive force
questions.explain: Constant velocity means zero resultant force, so the driving force balances the resistive forces.

questions.q: In which type of collision is kinetic energy conserved?
questions.explain: Kinetic energy is conserved only in perfectly elastic collisions; momentum is conserved in all of them.

questions.q: A motor lifts a 50 kg load at constant speed through 10 m in 20 s. The useful power output is: (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
Two forces of 3 N and 4 N act at right angles to each other. The magnitude of the resultant is:
questions.explain: For perpendicular vectors the resultant is √(3²+4²) = 5 N.

questions.q: A couple consists of:
options: Two equal, antiparallel forces not acting in the same line
Two equal, parallel forces acting in the same direction
questions.explain: A couple is a pair of equal, opposite, parallel forces whose lines of action differ, producing a turning effect.

questions.q: The work done by a constant force is given by:
questions.explain: Work equals force times displacement in the direction of the force, W = Fs cosθ.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, whereas speed, distance and mass are scalars.

questions.q: Why does a crumple zone reduce the force on car occupants in a crash?
options: It increases the change in momentum
It increases the mass of the car
It increases the time over which momentum changes
questions.explain: A longer contact time reduces the rate of change of momentum and hence the force (F = Δp/Δt).

questions.q: Newton's second law is most fundamentally expressed as:
questions.explain: Force equals the rate of change of momentum, F = Δp/Δt; F = ma is the special case of constant mass.

questions.q: A 0.50 kg ball moving at 4.0 m s⁻¹ rebounds at 4.0 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction. The magnitude of the change in momentum is:
On a displacement–time graph, the gradient at a point represents:
questions.explain: The gradient of a displacement–time graph is the instantaneous velocity.

questions.q: Which quantity is conserved in every collision in an isolated system?
questions.explain: Total linear momentum is always conserved when no external resultant force acts.

questions.q: The impulse of a force is equal to:
questions.explain: Impulse FΔt equals the change in momentum Δp.

questions.q: A force of 10 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. What is its horizontal component?
questions.explain: The horizontal component is the adjacent side, F cos30° ≈ 8.7 N.

questions.q: On a velocity–time graph, the area under the line represents:
questions.explain: The area under a velocity–time graph gives the displacement.

questions.q: Newton's first law states that a body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless:
options: A resultant force acts on it
questions.explain: A body's motion only changes when acted on by a non-zero resultant (net) force.

questions.q: Electrical energy transferred is given by E = VIt. For 5.0 V, 2.0 A flowing for 10 s, the energy is:
A 0.15 kg cricket ball is struck and its velocity changes by 30 m s⁻¹ over 0.010 s. The average force on the ball is:
Which component allows significant current to flow in only one direction, with a forward 'threshold' voltage of around 0.6 V?
questions.explain: A semiconductor diode conducts only in forward bias above its threshold voltage and blocks reverse current.

questions.q: In a potential divider, the output pd across resistor R₂ (in series with R₁ across supply V_in) is:
questions.explain: The output across R₂ is V_in × R₂/(R₁ + R₂).

questions.q: For a projectile launched on level ground, which launch angle gives the maximum range (no air resistance)?
questions.explain: Maximum horizontal range occurs at a launch angle of 45° on level ground.

questions.q: For an object in complete equilibrium under several forces:
options: The forces must all be equal
The resultant force is zero and the resultant moment is zero
questions.explain: Equilibrium requires both zero resultant force and zero resultant moment.

questions.q: According to Newton's third law, action and reaction forces:
options: Are the same type only by coincidence
Are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction on different bodies
questions.explain: Third-law pairs are equal, opposite, of the same type, and act on two different bodies.

questions.q: The moment of a force about a pivot is calculated as:
questions.explain: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action.

questions.q: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series. The total resistance is:
questions.explain: In series resistances simply add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω.

questions.q: An electric current of 2.0 A flows for 90 s. How much charge passes a point in the circuit?
A 12 V battery drives a current of 3.0 A through a resistor. Assuming negligible internal resistance, what is the resistance?
At a junction, currents of 3.0 A and 2.0 A flow in, and a 1.5 A branch flows out. The remaining outgoing current is:
questions.explain: By Kirchhoff's first law, in = out: 3.0 + 2.0 = 1.5 + I, so I = 3.5 A.
